triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

Triage: lands in `domain:server` (plugin-auth OAuth, MCP authorization) · `pm:queue`; rationale: area:ai · Feature (offer the RFC 8628 device authorization grant to MCP clients and declare it in the authorization-server metadata, so a client on a remote or headless machine completes OAuth without a localhost redirect; `objectstack login` already uses `/api/v1/auth/device/code`) · filed on the maintainer's word 「立卡」 after a remote MCP client failed OAuth on a hosted environment → p2 (a maintainer-sourced Feature; he may raise it) · size M.

repo:objectstack#6 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcSPM86QhYAcidhG5Bu

## 维护者速读

- 问题：AI 客户端跑在云端电脑上、用户在手机上点同意时，授权结果被送去手机自己的本机地址，页面打不开，只能把地址栏的网址手抄回客户端。只见过你演示的那一次；这类客户端每次连接都会遇到。
- 选项：A 增加“设备码授权”，客户端显示短码、用户在任意屏幕输入并同意，约 3 个 PR，只对会用设备码的客户端生效；B 现在不做，卡挂起，等有客户端确实会用设备码再做，用户照旧手抄；C 同意页在手机上不再跳去打不开的地址，改成“复制链接”一步，1 个小 PR。
- 推荐 B：实测通用的 AI 客户端开发包里没有设备码授权，也没有证据说明出问题的那个客户端会用它，现在做等于给每个环境多开一扇没人走的门。
- 不定会怎样：现状不变，远程客户端的用户授权后看到浏览器报错页，手抄网址才能连上。

## Decision analysis: a second way to approve an AI app that runs on another machine

**Question.** A person approves an AI app from a phone while the app runs on a cloud computer, lands on a page that cannot open, and copies the address back by hand: should the platform add an approval that needs no redirect?

**Background.** The card's premise (the platform already has this; open it to MCP clients) does not hold as measured: the existing short-code sign-in mints a full sign-in session, not the scoped agent grant.

Governing text: `packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts:63-79` (the switch is "CLI / TV-style login"; `/device/token` is "poll for the issued session token"); ruling 6232069920 A at `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:707-745` (a consent binds the approving session's organization, never a guessed one); objectstack-ai/cloud#3606 ruling A at `mcp-token-revocation.ts:251-259`, same directory (the consent is the revocable record the MCP door reads); `docs/NORTH-STAR.md:11` (road step "connect an agent"). No option conflicts with these; A must satisfy both rulings.

**Protocol.** A adds public surface: a token-endpoint grant, a discovery key, a registrable grant, two columns on `sys_device_code`, a new meaning for the spec switch. B and C add none.

**Premises** (origin/main 30b0987c, committed 2026-11-21T15:25Z; "run" = executed on better-auth and @better-auth/oauth-provider 1.7.12, tarballs matching the lockfile; `A=packages/plugins/plugin-auth`, `P=ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth`):

1. Discovery today lists three grants and no device endpoint, and self-registration silently drops a requested device grant (run). The document is the vendor's (`$A/src/auth-plugin.ts:6251-6255`). Re-check: `git grep -l "oauthDeviceAuthorization\|device_authorization_endpoint" origin/main | wc -l` → 0 (control: `git grep -c deviceAuthorization origin/main -- $A/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts` → 5).
2. The existing flow is the vendor's plain plugin, off by default, no environment switch (`auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:237`, `:996-1002`). Not gated to the CLI: an unregistered client name gets a code, and approval yields a full session, not a scoped grant (run). Vendor defaults: 8-character code (40 bits), 30 min expiry, 5 s polling interval, single use (run). Re-check: `git grep -n validateClient origin/main -- $A/src | wc -l` → 0.
3. The pinned vendor ships its own OAuth device grant. Switched on with nothing else (run): discovery advertises it; an anonymous client registers for it with no redirect address; the first-party name `objectstack-cli` (`packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:422`, `packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts:751`) is refused; the token carries no organization and leaves no consent record, though the approving session had one. The MCP door refuses a token with no consent (`mcp-token-revocation.ts:277`; read, not run). Re-check: `grep -n "function oauthDeviceAuthorization" $A/node_modules/@better-auth/oauth-provider/dist/index.mjs`.
4. The consent page names the app, marks it unverified, names where the grant goes and lists permissions (`$P/OAuthConsentPage.tsx:190`, `:392`, `:438`). The device page shows none of these (`DeviceAuthPage.tsx:56`, `:299-309`), and a device request has no destination to show. Re-check: `git grep -n "client_id\|scope" origin/main -- $P/DeviceAuthPage.tsx | wc -l` → 0.
5. No reader is measured: the pinned MCP client kit (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.1) contains no device grant. Re-check: `grep -rIlE "device_code|device_authorization" node_modules/.pnpm/@modelcontextprotocol+sdk@1.32.1*/ | wc -l` → 0.
6. The consent page leaves for any web address, loopback included; its stay-and-finish card covers app links only. Re-check: `git grep -n "window.location.assign(redirect)" origin/main -- $P/OAuthConsentPage.tsx` → line 264.

| Option | What ships | What the customer sees | Workload |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | The vendor's device grant behind the existing switch; its approval page names the app, the unverified mark and the permissions; approval writes the same consent record with the organization; the first-party name keeps working | An app that speaks the grant shows a short code, approved on any screen; other apps see no change. Any self-registered app can start a request where the switch is on | server + ui lanes · 3 PRs · switch and pin like #25156 (+405/−0); page like #32053 (+961/−10); consent and organization on this path: no precedent (nearest #30879, +1114/−16) |
| B | Nothing; the card goes on hold with a restart condition | As today | 0 PRs |
| C | On a phone or tablet, a grant headed to a loopback address stops on a card with Copy link and Continue | One tap, then paste into the app; works in apps that accept a pasted link (the sighted one did) | ui lane · 1 PR · #34369 (+264/−9) |

**In business terms.** A: a TV-style pairing code beside the sign-in redirect. B: keep the manual step until an app can use a code. C: put the claim ticket on screen so the person can carry it over.

**Four axes.**

- Long-term soundness. In two years an agent on any machine is approved through one consent record on one approval page. GitHub, Salesforce and Microsoft Entra offer a device code as a per-application opt-in, and Entra advises blocking it unless a device needs it, because approval is not tied to the machine that asked (general knowledge, not measured here). A is that shape once apps use it; today it adds that surface and a second approval page that must track the first, for no measured user.
- Business pull. One sighting, with a working manual step; nothing measured asks for a device code.
- AI-error guard. A built halfway fails loudly (the agent and the command-line sign-in are refused), with one quiet case: a grant with no organization. C fails loudly (a stale link).
- No spread. A is permanent surface on every host with the switch on; C is one page branch; B is nothing.

os-decision-facets
① Long-term soundness: A widens the contract and adds a second approval page; B adds nothing; C adds one page branch.
② Business pull: one sighting; no measured client requests a device code.
③ AI-error guard: A refuses loudly except for a missing organization; B and C move no boundary.
④ No spread: A is a standing obligation with no user today; B none; C small.
Prior rulings read: device authorization,device_code,rfc 8628,deviceauthorization,device flow,loopback redirect,dynamic client registration,oauth consent → 0 hits; ADR-0090 D10 (read; it governs who the agent is, not how it is approved); thread: none

**Recommendation: B.** Not A: nothing measured would use it, and it is three PRs on the sign-in boundary, three times C. Not C: it tidies the hand copy by guessing the device, on one sighting.

Confidence gaps: whether the sighted client, or any client the maintainer's users run, speaks the device grant is not verified (only the reference client kit was read; the MCP specification site was unreachable here); whether the hosted environment has the switch on was not read; the door's refusal in premise 3 is read, not run.

Self-check: axis ① alone picks B; do ②③④ flip it: no.

**After the ruling.**

- B: the seat puts the card on hold; it restarts when a named MCP client is shown requesting a device code from a server it discovered.
- A: the same ruling settles two points: whether any self-registered app may use it (marked unverified) or only administrator-registered ones, and whether hosted environments turn the switch on. Then three PRs in the table's order, the card's security reading in the first. The dev re-runs premise 3 first; if the organization cannot ride the vendor path without copying vendor internals, the dev reports the fork and ships nothing.
- C: a new ui card; this card goes on hold as in B.

Related: #24218 (the organization binding A must match).
